item.content:encoded:
The African Institute for Mathematical Sciences (AIMS) is inviting applications for the position of Program Manager at AIMS Rwanda, based at its Centre of Excellence in Kigali, Rwanda. This is a full-time opportunity for an experienced program and project management professional who wants to contribute to Africa’s scientific, educational, and economic development.

The Program Manager will provide operational leadership and coordination for AIMS Rwanda’s programs, including the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program and other donor-funded initiatives. The successful candidate will also contribute to partnerships, fundraising, program implementation, budgeting, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, and the long-term sustainability of the Centre.

Applications will be accepted until August 31, 2026.

Opportunity Overview

  • Organization: African Institute for Mathematical Sciences (AIMS)
  • Position: Program Manager, AIMS Rwanda
  • Location: Kigali, Rwanda
  • Centre: AIMS Rwanda Centre of Excellence
  • Employment type: Full-time
  • Functional focus: Program management, partnerships, fundraising, education and development
  • Application deadline: August 31, 2026
  • Reporting to: Centre President
  • Primary working environment: Multicultural and international
  • Languages: Excellent English required; French is an advantage

About the African Institute for Mathematical Sciences

The African Institute for Mathematical Sciences (AIMS) is a pan-African network of centres of excellence dedicated to postgraduate education, research, and public engagement in mathematical sciences and STEM.

AIMS was established with the goal of enabling Africa’s brightest students to develop the skills, knowledge, and independent thinking required to contribute to Africa’s scientific, educational, and economic development.

The first AIMS Centre was established in Cape Town, South Africa, in 2003. Since then, the network has expanded across the continent, with Centres in:

  • South Africa
  • Senegal
  • Ghana
  • Cameroon
  • Rwanda

AIMS currently operates two Centres in Rwanda, contributing to the organisation’s broader pan-African network.

Each AIMS Centre provides tailored academic and non-academic programs and trains approximately 50 African students each year, preparing them for leadership roles in areas including academia, government, and industry.

The AIMS academic model also brings together leading international lecturers who teach within an intensive 24-hour learning environment.

About the AIMS Rwanda Program Manager Position

The Program Manager will be based at the AIMS Rwanda Centre in Kigali and will report directly to the Centre President.

The central responsibility of the role is to coordinate and oversee the day-to-day programmatic activities of the Centre.

This includes responsibility for the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program as well as other programs and activities funded by donors.

The position goes beyond routine program administration. The successful candidate will also help AIMS Rwanda strengthen its partnership network, support fundraising activities, and contribute to revenue-generating initiatives designed to support the long-term sustainability of the Centre.

The Program Manager will therefore play an important role in ensuring that AIMS Rwanda’s programs are properly planned, implemented, monitored, evaluated, and reported.

Key Responsibilities of the Program Manager

1. Program Coordination

The Program Manager will coordinate the Centre’s day-to-day programmatic activities.

This involves ensuring that programs are implemented effectively and remain aligned with their intended objectives.

Responsibilities may include:

  • Coordinating program activities
  • Supporting program planning
  • Monitoring implementation
  • Ensuring activities are delivered on time
  • Identifying implementation challenges
  • Developing solutions to program-related issues
  • Coordinating different teams and stakeholders
  • Ensuring program objectives are achieved

The position requires someone who can manage multiple activities while maintaining a strong focus on results.

2. Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program

A significant part of the position involves supporting the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at AIMS Rwanda.

The Program Manager will contribute to ensuring that the program is effectively coordinated and implemented.

This requires strong organizational, monitoring, reporting, stakeholder-management, and program-management abilities.

Because the program involves students and education, the role also requires an understanding of the broader relationship between education, development, and opportunities for young people in Africa.

3. Management of Donor-Funded Programs

The Program Manager will oversee and coordinate other donor-funded programs and activities implemented through AIMS Rwanda.

This requires an understanding of donor expectations and the ability to ensure that programs meet agreed objectives, timelines, budgets, and reporting requirements.

The successful candidate will need to be comfortable working within donor-funded environments and managing the associated accountability requirements.

4. Planning and Budget Management

The position includes responsibility for operational leadership in planning and budgeting.

The Program Manager will work with the relevant teams to ensure that programs have appropriate plans and budgets and that implementation is monitored against those plans.

Strong financial management and organizational skills are therefore important.

Candidates should be comfortable working with budgets and using tools such as Microsoft Excel to support program planning and reporting.

5. Monitoring, Evaluation and Reporting

Monitoring, evaluation, and reporting are important components of this role.

The Program Manager should have a high level of comfort with Results Based Management (RBM), monitoring and evaluation (M&E), and program reporting.

This means the successful candidate should be able to:

  • Establish and monitor program objectives
  • Track progress against expected results
  • Analyze program performance
  • Identify challenges and areas requiring improvement
  • Support impact measurement
  • Prepare accurate reports
  • Communicate program results to stakeholders and donors

The ability to translate program data into meaningful information for decision-making will be particularly valuable.

6. Impact Evaluation

The position requires experience and understanding of the impact evaluation requirements associated with foundations and international donors.

AIMS specifically identifies experience with donors such as:

  • Canadian Government
  • Global Affairs Canada (GAC)
  • International Development Research Centre (IDRC)
  • UKaid
  • USAID
  • Other government and international development agencies

Experience working within donor-funded programs and understanding donor reporting and impact requirements can therefore strengthen an applicant’s profile.

7. Partnership Development

The Program Manager will also support the Centre President in developing a strong and sustainable partnership network.

These partnerships may exist at both:

  • National level
  • International level

The role therefore requires someone who can communicate effectively with different stakeholders and develop constructive professional relationships.

Strong networking and interpersonal skills will be important for building and maintaining partnerships that support AIMS Rwanda’s objectives.

8. Fundraising and Resource Mobilization

The Program Manager will actively contribute to fundraising initiatives.

This may involve identifying opportunities and supporting efforts to secure resources for the Centre’s programs and operations.

The position also includes contributing to revenue-generating activities aimed at ensuring the long-term sustainability of AIMS Rwanda’s operations.

Candidates who have experience in fundraising, resource mobilization, donor engagement, or partnership development may therefore have an advantage.

9. Operational Leadership

The Program Manager will provide operational leadership and oversight across the Centre’s program activities.

This requires the ability to coordinate different functions while ensuring that programs remain on track.

The role will involve working closely with a multicultural team and interacting with students, staff, partners, donors, and members of the wider public.

10. Problem-Solving and Decision-Making

AIMS is looking for someone who can make sound decisions and exercise good judgment.

The successful candidate should be capable of identifying challenges during program implementation and developing practical solutions.

This requires:

  • Independent thinking
  • Analytical skills
  • Good judgment
  • Creativity
  • Flexibility
  • A results-oriented approach

The role is suited to someone who can take ownership of responsibilities rather than waiting to be directed at every stage.

Educational Requirements

Applicants should have a Master’s degree in one of the following areas or a related discipline:

  • International Development
  • Economics
  • Business Administration
  • Project Management
  • Social Sciences
  • Education

An equivalent qualification may also be considered.

The academic background should provide a strong foundation for program management, development work, education, business, economics, or related areas.

Professional Experience Requirements

Applicants must have a minimum of five years of professional experience in program and budget management.

This experience should include responsibility for areas such as:

  • Day-to-day program implementation
  • Program monitoring
  • Budget management
  • Program coordination
  • Operational planning
  • Reporting
  • Program performance

The requirement for five years of experience means that this is an experienced professional-level position rather than an entry-level opportunity.

Project and Program Management Qualifications

Professional qualifications in project or program management are expected.

Examples specifically mentioned by AIMS include:

  • PgMP
  • PMP
  • MSP

Candidates with recognized professional project or program management credentials should highlight them prominently in their applications.

STEM and Education Experience

AIMS is particularly interested in candidates who have an understanding of education and development in Africa, with a strong focus on Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) education.

Experience in education programs, STEM initiatives, development projects, or related areas can therefore be highly relevant.

This is particularly important because AIMS’s core mission is focused on mathematical sciences, STEM education, research, and the development of Africa’s scientific talent.

Gender Equity and Equality

An appreciation of, or training in, gender equity and equality is also identified as a requirement.

Applicants should therefore demonstrate awareness of the importance of inclusive and equitable approaches within education and development programs.

Communication and Language Skills

Excellent communication skills are required.

Applicants must be able to communicate effectively in English, both orally and in writing.

This is important because the position involves:

  • Program reporting
  • Stakeholder communication
  • Donor engagement
  • Partnership development
  • Facilitation
  • Team coordination
  • Presentations
  • Interaction with students and staff

A working knowledge of French is an added advantage.

Multicultural Working Environment

AIMS operates across several African countries and works with students, lecturers, researchers, development partners, and professionals from different backgrounds.

The Program Manager must therefore be comfortable working within a multicultural environment.

AIMS is looking for someone with strong interpersonal skills who can effectively interact with:

  • Multicultural teams
  • Students from different backgrounds
  • Staff
  • Partners
  • Donors
  • Members of the public

The ability to work respectfully and effectively across different cultures and backgrounds is an important part of the position.

Results-Oriented Approach

The successful candidate should be highly results-driven and motivated by a strong commitment to performance excellence.

AIMS is looking for someone who can:

  • Set clear objectives
  • Establish realistic deadlines
  • Monitor progress
  • Deliver results
  • Respond quickly to challenges
  • Maintain high standards

A strong sense of urgency and accountability will be important in managing the Centre’s programs.

Entrepreneurial Mindset

AIMS is also looking for an entrepreneurial and self-starting professional.

The successful candidate should enjoy working in a dynamic environment and be comfortable identifying opportunities rather than simply responding to instructions.

This quality is particularly relevant to the fundraising and revenue-generation aspects of the position.

Technical Skills

Applicants should be proficient in the Microsoft Office Suite, including:

  • Microsoft Excel
  • Microsoft PowerPoint
  • Microsoft Word

Knowledge of internet-based applications such as Skype, Gmail, and similar digital tools is also expected.

Strong Excel skills can be particularly useful for program budgets, monitoring data, reporting, and analysis.

Who Should Apply?

This position is particularly suited to experienced professionals who have a combination of:

  • A relevant Master’s degree
  • At least five years of program and budget management experience
  • Professional project/program management qualifications
  • Experience with donor-funded programs
  • Knowledge of monitoring and evaluation
  • Results Based Management experience
  • Strong communication skills
  • Partnership development experience
  • Fundraising or resource mobilization experience
  • Experience in education and development
  • Knowledge of STEM education in Africa
  • Strong organizational and leadership abilities

Candidates who have worked with major international donors or development agencies may be particularly well positioned for the role.

APPLY HERE

Why Consider the AIMS Rwanda Program Manager Opportunity?

The position offers the opportunity to contribute directly to an organisation whose mission is centered on developing Africa’s scientific and mathematical talent.

The successful candidate will not only manage programs but also contribute to broader objectives involving:

  • African scientific development
  • STEM education
  • Postgraduate education
  • Youth development
  • International partnerships
  • Donor-funded initiatives
  • Resource mobilization
  • Sustainable institutional development

The position could therefore be particularly valuable for an experienced program manager interested in combining management, education, international development, STEM, and African development.

Visit HERE to learn more about the AIMS Rwanda Program Manager Job 2026 in Kigali

Location: Kigali, Rwanda

The position is based at the AIMS Rwanda Centre in Kigali, Rwanda.

Kigali serves as the operational base for the role, meaning the successful candidate will be expected to work from the AIMS Rwanda Centre as part of its full-time operations.

Employment Type

This is a full-time opportunity.

The Program Manager will be integrated into the AIMS Rwanda Centre and will work closely with the Centre President and the wider AIMS team.

Equal Opportunity Employer

AIMS states that it is an equal opportunity employer.

The organisation encourages qualified professionals to apply and is committed to considering candidates based on their qualifications, skills, experience, and suitability for the position.

Application Deadline

Applications will be accepted until:

August 31, 2026

Applicants are encouraged to submit their applications before the deadline and ensure that all required information and supporting documents are complete.

Application and Recruitment Information

Interested candidates should apply through the official AIMS recruitment process and carefully review the requirements before submitting their application.

Candidates should ensure their CV and application clearly demonstrate:

  • Academic qualifications
  • Professional experience
  • Program management experience
  • Budget management experience
  • Project/program management certification
  • Donor experience
  • M&E and RBM experience
  • Partnership experience
  • Fundraising experience
  • STEM or education experience
  • Leadership and communication skills

AIMS notes that if applicants do not receive feedback within five weeks after the application deadline, they should consider that their application will not be pursued further.

AIMS also reserves the right not to make an appointment at its sole discretion.

Conclusion

The AIMS Rwanda Program Manager position in Kigali is a significant professional opportunity for an experienced program and project management specialist interested in contributing to Africa’s scientific, educational, and economic development.

The successful candidate will provide day-to-day programmatic leadership, oversee donor-funded initiatives including the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program, manage budgets and implementation, support monitoring and evaluation, contribute to reporting, develop partnerships, and assist with fundraising and revenue-generating initiatives.

Applicants should have a Master’s degree in a relevant field, at least five years of professional experience in program and budget management, and professional project or program management qualifications such as PMP, PgMP, or MSP. Experience with international donors, STEM education, development programs, partnerships, fundraising, and monitoring and evaluation will be highly relevant.

For professionals passionate about African development, education, STEM, program management, and creating opportunities for Africa’s next generation of scientific leaders, this position offers an opportunity to contribute to the work of a major pan-African network of centres of excellence.

Application deadline: August 31, 2026.

item.content:encoded:
Are you a recent graduate looking to build practical experience in communications, social media management, digital content, website publishing, and events? Friends of Europe is offering a six-month paid Communications Assistant traineeship designed to help early-career professionals develop hands-on communications experience while working within an influential European think tank.

The traineeship provides an opportunity to work across social media, digital communications, publications, website management, multimedia content, events, campaigns, podcasts, and communications administration.

The position is based in Belgium and operates under a hybrid working arrangement. The traineeship is expected to begin in late September or early October 2026 and will run for six months, with the possibility of renewal.

The application deadline is August 26, 2026, at 23:59 CEST.

Opportunity Overview

  • Organisation: Friends of Europe
  • Position: Communications Assistant
  • Opportunity type: Paid traineeship
  • Duration: 6 months
  • Expected start: Late September/early October 2026
  • Location: Belgium
  • Work arrangement: Hybrid
  • Team: Communications
  • Application deadline: August 26, 2026 at 23:59 CEST
  • Application requirement: CV in PDF format, no longer than two pages
  • Selection process: One-hour online test followed by an interview for shortlisted candidates
  • Possibility of renewal: Yes

About Friends of Europe

Friends of Europe is an independent think tank focused on policymaking and international cooperation.

The organisation works toward a multilateral world where different levels of government, businesses, civil society organisations, and citizens can cooperate to address common challenges.

Friends of Europe believes that effective policies and innovative ideas can emerge through collaboration, breaking down traditional silos, and creating communities based on trust.

Founded in 1999, the organisation works to stimulate debate, connect people, and encourage change in support of a more inclusive, sustainable, and forward-looking Europe.

About the Communications Assistant Traineeship

The Communications Assistant will join the Communications Team and support a broad range of communications activities.

The traineeship is designed for people who have recently graduated and are looking to gain their first significant professional experience.

Rather than being solely an observational internship, Friends of Europe describes its traineeships as an opportunity to combine initial full-time work experience with hands-on training.

During the six-month programme, the successful candidate will have the opportunity to develop practical skills while contributing directly to the organisation’s communications work.

This could be particularly valuable for graduates interested in careers involving:

  • Communications
  • Social media management
  • Digital marketing
  • Content creation
  • Journalism
  • Public relations
  • Website management
  • Policy communications
  • Multimedia production
  • Events
  • European affairs
  • International development
  • Think tanks and public policy

What Will the Communications Assistant Do?

The successful candidate will work across several areas of Friends of Europe’s communications activities.

1. Editing Publications

The Communications Assistant will help edit publications produced by Friends of Europe.

This may include:

  • Articles
  • Reports
  • Other written publications

The candidate will be expected to ensure that content follows the organisation’s in-house style and maintains a high standard of written communication.

Strong English writing and editing abilities are therefore important for this role.

2. Social Media Management

Social media is a major part of the position.

The Communications Assistant will support the creation, planning, and scheduling of content across platforms including:

  • LinkedIn
  • Instagram
  • Bluesky

Responsibilities may include drafting social media posts, adapting visual materials, planning content, and supporting live event coverage.

This means the role provides practical experience in managing social media communications within a professional policy-focused organisation.

Candidates who already have experience managing social media accounts, creating content, writing captions, designing visuals, or analysing social media performance may find this particularly relevant.

3. Campaign Optimisation

The Communications Assistant will contribute to the daily optimisation of communications campaigns.

The goal will be to help campaigns perform effectively and achieve their intended objectives.

This requires an ability to:

  • Monitor campaign performance
  • Identify useful insights
  • Understand audience engagement
  • Adjust communications approaches
  • Support the achievement of campaign goals

This aspect of the traineeship can help candidates develop practical knowledge of digital campaign management and performance optimisation.

4. Research and Insights

The role also involves using different tools and information sources to uncover insights and develop strong messages.

The Communications Assistant may therefore need to research information, identify relevant trends, and help translate findings into effective communications.

Strong research, analytical, and information-gathering abilities can be valuable in this area.

5. Website Management

The successful candidate will assist with updating and publishing content on the Friends of Europe website using WordPress.

Tasks may include:

  • Updating website content
  • Formatting articles
  • Uploading publications
  • Publishing digital materials
  • Making basic SEO optimisations where appropriate

Experience with WordPress is an added advantage, although the role is also suitable for candidates interested in developing their website publishing skills.

6. Social Media and Website Analytics

The Communications Assistant will help extract data and develop performance reports relating to the organisation’s social media and website activities.

The purpose is not simply to collect numbers but to identify useful insights and lessons that can help improve future communications.

This provides an opportunity to develop experience with:

  • Social media analytics
  • Website performance
  • Data extraction
  • Performance reporting
  • Audience insights
  • Campaign evaluation

7. Multimedia Content

The role also involves supporting the production of multimedia content for Friends of Europe’s social media channels.

This can include:

  • Short-form videos
  • Event clips
  • Digital assets
  • Other multimedia materials

Candidates with experience in video editing, photography, graphic design, or Canva may therefore have an advantage.

8. Events and Live Coverage

Friends of Europe organises events related to European and global affairs.

The Communications Assistant may support communications around these events, including live coverage.

Because some events can take place in the morning, evening, or on weekends, candidates need to demonstrate flexibility when required.

9. Podcasts

The Communications Assistant will also assist with the conceptualisation, planning, and production of podcasts.

This provides exposure to another form of digital communication and allows the trainee to develop experience in multimedia storytelling and content production.

10. Administrative and Communications Support

The position also includes administrative responsibilities that support the Communications Team.

These may include:

  • Taking meeting minutes
  • Managing correspondence
  • Updating databases
  • Supporting press activities
  • Supporting multimedia projects
  • Completing other communications-related tasks as required

Skills and Qualities Friends of Europe Is Looking For

The organisation is looking for someone who is motivated, organised, flexible, and willing to take initiative.

Highly Motivated and Hands-On

The successful candidate should demonstrate enthusiasm for learning and be willing to take an active role in the team’s work.

A hands-on attitude is important because the traineeship is designed around practical experience.

Solution-Oriented Approach

Friends of Europe is looking for someone with a “can-do” and solution-oriented mentality.

Applicants should demonstrate that they are able to identify challenges and look for practical ways to solve them.

Attention to Detail

The Communications Assistant will work with written publications, social media posts, website content, reports, and other communications materials.

Being able to meet deadlines while maintaining accuracy and attention to detail is therefore essential.

Ability to Work Independently

The candidate should be comfortable working both as part of a multicultural team and with minimal supervision.

This requires initiative, responsibility, communication, and good organisational skills.

Interest in Think Tanks

Applicants should have a genuine interest in working for a think tank.

An understanding of how think tanks contribute to policy discussions and public debate can help candidates succeed in the role.

Flexibility

The position may sometimes require attendance at events during mornings, evenings, or weekends.

Candidates should therefore be willing to work flexibly when required by communications and event activities.

Education and Experience Requirements

Applicants should have demonstrable knowledge of and interest in communications.

This can come from:

  • A relevant degree
  • Equivalent experience
  • Self-learning
  • Practical communications experience

The organisation also welcomes candidates who have developed communications skills through practical experience outside of formal education.

English Language Requirement

Fluent English is required.

The vacancy specifies that written and spoken English at native-level fluency is required.

Excellent writing skills are particularly important because the role involves editing publications, drafting social media content, preparing communications materials, and supporting various written outputs.

Social Media Experience

An interest in social media is required, while previous experience is considered an advantage.

Candidates should have basic knowledge of:

  • Social media platforms
  • Social media management tools
  • Social media analytics

Experience creating and managing content for platforms such as LinkedIn, Instagram, and other social networks can therefore strengthen an application.

Graphic Design and Digital Skills

Friends of Europe identifies several additional skills as an advantage.

These include:

  • Graphic design
  • Photography
  • Canva
  • Video editing
  • WordPress

Applicants do not necessarily need to be experts in all these areas, but having practical experience in some of them can make a candidate’s application stronger.

Interest in European and Global Affairs

Applicants should have knowledge of and an interest in European and global affairs.

This is particularly important because Friends of Europe is a think tank focused on European policymaking, international cooperation, and global challenges.

Candidates should therefore demonstrate an interest in current affairs, policy, international relations, European issues, or related areas.

Who Can Apply?

The eligibility requirements for this traineeship are specific.

The position is open to:

  • Nationals of European Union member states
  • Nationals of European Economic Area (EEA) member states
  • Nationals of Switzerland
  • Non-EU nationals who already have the right to work in Belgium

Applicants who do not fall into these categories may not be eligible for the position because the organisation does not indicate that it will provide work authorization for candidates who do not already have the right to work in Belgium.

APPLY HERE

Profile of the Ideal Candidate

The opportunity is particularly suited to a recent graduate who wants to turn academic knowledge or self-developed digital skills into practical professional experience.

A strong candidate could have a combination of:

  • A relevant communications or related degree
  • Excellent English writing skills
  • Social media experience
  • Content creation skills
  • Digital marketing knowledge
  • Basic analytics experience
  • Graphic design skills
  • Canva experience
  • Video editing skills
  • WordPress experience
  • An interest in European and global affairs
  • Strong organisational skills
  • An ability to work independently
  • A willingness to learn

Candidates do not need to have extensive professional experience, as the traineeship is specifically designed for people who have recently graduated and are seeking initial full-time work experience.

What Makes This Traineeship Valuable?

One of the strongest aspects of the opportunity is its broad communications exposure.

Rather than focusing on just one area, the successful trainee can gain experience across several digital and traditional communications functions.

These include:

  1. Social media management
  2. Content creation
  3. Digital campaigns
  4. Website publishing
  5. Basic SEO
  6. Social media analytics
  7. Website analytics
  8. Publication editing
  9. Multimedia production
  10. Event communications
  11. Podcast production
  12. Database and administrative support

This broad exposure can help a recent graduate understand how a professional communications team operates and identify which areas of communications they may want to specialise in long term.

Hybrid Working Arrangement

The position is listed as hybrid, meaning the successful candidate will have a combination of workplace and remote-working arrangements according to the organisation’s working practices.

Candidates should be prepared to participate in team activities, meetings, and events as required.

Duration and Start Date

The traineeship is expected to begin in late September or early October 2026.

The initial traineeship will last six months, with a possibility of renewal.

This provides a substantial period for the successful candidate to gain practical experience and build a professional portfolio.

Application Requirements

Applicants are required to apply through the Friends of Europe website.

The application should include a CV in PDF format.

The CV should be:

  • No longer than two pages
  • Focused on relevant skills and experience
  • Clear and well structured
  • Tailored to the Communications Assistant position

Applicants should also answer the relevant application questions and demonstrate their motivation for applying.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Communications Assistant Paid Traineeship at Friends of Europe in Belgium

Selection Process

The recruitment process includes multiple stages.

Stage 1: Application

Candidates submit their application, including their CV and responses to the relevant questions.

Stage 2: Online Test

Shortlisted candidates will be invited to complete a one-hour online test.

Applicants should therefore be prepared to demonstrate their communications, writing, analytical, and practical skills.

Stage 3: Interview

Candidates who successfully progress through the test stage will be invited for an interview.

The interview provides an opportunity for Friends of Europe to assess the candidate’s experience, motivation, skills, and suitability for the role.

Application Deadline

The deadline for applications is:

August 26, 2026, at 23:59 CEST.

Applicants should submit their applications before the deadline. Waiting until the final hours can create unnecessary risks, particularly if there are technical issues with the application platform.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should visit the official Friends of Europe recruitment page, answer the required application questions, and upload their CV in PDF format.

When preparing your application, it is advisable to highlight relevant experience in:

  • Communications
  • Social media
  • Content creation
  • Digital marketing
  • Writing and editing
  • Website publishing
  • WordPress
  • Canva
  • Graphic design
  • Video production
  • Analytics
  • Events
  • European and global affairs

Applicants should also clearly communicate why they are interested in working for a think tank and how the traineeship fits into their professional development goals.

Conclusion

The Friends of Europe Communications Assistant traineeship offers recent graduates an opportunity to gain six months of practical, paid experience within an established European think tank.

The position provides broad exposure to social media management, digital content creation, publication editing, website publishing, basic SEO, analytics, multimedia production, events, podcasts, and communications campaigns.

Candidates with strong English writing skills, an interest in communications, knowledge of social media, and an interest in European and global affairs are encouraged to consider the opportunity. Additional skills in graphic design, photography, Canva, video editing, and WordPress can further strengthen an application.

Because the traineeship is specifically designed for people seeking their first professional experience after graduation, it can be a valuable stepping stone for anyone looking to establish a career in communications, digital media, public affairs, policy communications, or related fields.

The application deadline is August 26, 2026, at 23:59 CEST, and eligible candidates should ensure their application and two-page CV are submitted before the deadline.

For more global grants, scholarships, fellowships, internships, jobs, conferences, competitions, and other career opportunities for young people, visit the Opportunities for Youth (OFY) website at www.opportunitiesforyouth.org.

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is inviting applications for Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3, a seven-week online learning and volunteer opportunity designed to help participants strengthen their leadership capacity and identify how they can contribute to achieving Agenda 2063: The Africa We Want.

The programme provides participants with practical tools to move beyond simply understanding Agenda 2063 and instead identify the influence, opportunities and responsibilities they have within their own “Power Spaces” — including governments, businesses, universities, communities, schools, development organizations, families and professional networks.

The opportunity is conducted entirely online and requires approximately 11–15 hours per week.

About the Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces Programme

Agenda 2063 represents Africa’s long-term development vision and focuses on building The Africa We Want. However, achieving this vision requires more than awareness of continental development frameworks.

The UNDP-led programme focuses on helping participants recognize that meaningful transformation can take place through the everyday environments where people make decisions, influence others, and create value.

These environments are referred to as “Power Spaces.”

The programme therefore encourages participants to ask:

  • What contribution can I make to Africa’s transformation?
  • What future am I committed to creating?
  • What needs to change to achieve that future?
  • What leadership values do I need?
  • What actions should I consistently take?
  • What would success look like?
  • How can I continue improving after the programme?

What Participants Will Learn

During the seven-week journey, participants will develop seven practical leadership tools:

1. Contribution Statement

Participants identify the value they currently create through their Power Space and consider how their work, activities or influence can contribute to Africa’s transformation.

2. Moonshot

Participants define an ambitious and meaningful future they are committed to helping create rather than simply accepting current circumstances.

3. Delivery

Participants identify the important changes required to move from their current situation toward their desired future.

4. Leadership Values

Participants explore the values they need to guide important decisions and actions throughout their leadership journey.

5. Leadership Routines

Participants translate their intentions into practical and repeatable behaviours that can gradually produce meaningful results.

6. Letter from the Future

Participants imagine their desired future as if it has already been achieved and use that perspective to reconsider the choices they are making today.

7. Future Review

Participants learn a continuous improvement approach based on:

Return → Review → Revise → Recommit

This enables them to continue using the programme’s leadership tools after the formal seven-week experience has ended.

What Will Online Volunteers Do?

Selected Online Volunteers will participate in the learning experience while also supporting the delivery and improvement of the cohort.

Their responsibilities will include:

  • Studying the Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces Reader and related learning materials.
  • Supporting participant engagement throughout the seven-week programme.
  • Becoming familiar with weekly concepts, questions and exercises.
  • Participating in small-group learning conversations where assigned.
  • Helping participants connect the leadership tools to their own Power Spaces and circumstances.
  • Providing constructive and concise feedback.
  • Contributing to the end-of-cohort review.
  • Identifying what worked well and suggesting areas that could improve future cohorts.

Importantly, applicants do not need to be experts on every aspect of Agenda 2063. The programme emphasizes curiosity, disciplined engagement with the provided materials and the willingness to help others apply the concepts to their own contexts.

Programme Format and Time Commitment

This is a fully online opportunity, meaning volunteers can participate remotely.

Duration: 7 weeks
Modality: Online
Time commitment: 11–15 hours per week
Host organization: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)
Assignment country: Ethiopia
Sustainable Development Goal: SDG 17 – Partnerships for the Goals
Recruitment: Competitive

The assignment focuses on learning, participant engagement, leadership development and contributing to the improvement of future cohorts.

Who Should Apply?

The opportunity is particularly suitable for people who have a strong interest in areas such as:

  • Agenda 2063 and Africa’s development
  • Leadership and development practice
  • Public policy
  • Business and entrepreneurship
  • Education
  • Community development
  • Social impact
  • African transformation

Applicants may come from different professional and educational backgrounds. The programme specifically welcomes:

  • Professionals
  • Development practitioners
  • Researchers
  • Entrepreneurs
  • Educators
  • Students
  • Community leaders

Applicants should also demonstrate strong written and interpersonal communication skills and the ability to engage critically with learning materials.

Required Skills and Experience

Candidates should demonstrate:

  1. Strong interest in African development and Agenda 2063 or related areas.
  2. Critical reading skills and the ability to engage meaningfully with learning materials.
  3. Strong written and interpersonal communication skills.
  4. Ability to provide concise and constructive feedback.
  5. Commitment to completing the assignment throughout the seven-week Cohort 3 period.

Language Requirement

English: Fluent level is desirable.

Important Application Information

The recruitment is competitive, and applicants should be prepared to commit to the full duration of the assignment.

Application deadline: 4 September 2026 at 03:00.

The programme is expected to run for seven weeks, with participants working remotely and contributing approximately 11–15 hours per week.

Click HERE to read more and apply.

Why This Opportunity Is Valuable

The Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces programme can provide participants with an opportunity to:

  • Develop practical leadership skills.
  • Better understand their potential contribution to Africa’s long-term development.
  • Connect personal leadership with Agenda 2063.
  • Strengthen communication and collaboration skills.
  • Learn how to turn ideas into practical action.
  • Engage with people working across different sectors and Power Spaces.
  • Develop a personal leadership portfolio and future-oriented leadership practice.
  • Contribute feedback that can help improve future cohorts.

The programme is particularly relevant for individuals who want to connect their career, community involvement, education, entrepreneurship or professional influence with broader African development goals.

Conclusion

The UNDP Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3 offers a structured seven-week online leadership journey for individuals interested in contributing to Africa’s transformation. Rather than focusing only on theoretical knowledge of Agenda 2063, the programme encourages participants to identify their own areas of influence and develop practical ways to create value within them.

With a commitment of 11–15 hours per week and a deadline of 4 September 2026, interested applicants should review the requirements carefully and submit their applications before the recruitment period closes.

Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3

Are you passionate about Africa’s development, leadership, public policy, education, entrepreneurship, community development, or the long-term vision of The Africa We Want? The Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3 offers an opportunity to take part in a structured seven-week online learning and volunteer experience designed to help participants understand how they can contribute to Africa’s transformation within their own spheres of influence.

Hosted by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and delivered through the wider Agenda 2063 learning ecosystem, the programme focuses on turning knowledge of Agenda 2063 into practical individual leadership and action.

The online assignment is designed for people who want to explore their personal contribution to Africa’s development while supporting other participants during the seven-week traineeship. It does not require applicants to be experts on every aspect of Agenda 2063. Instead, it emphasizes curiosity, critical engagement, communication, willingness to learn, and the ability to help others connect ideas to their own real-world environments.

Opportunity Overview

  • Opportunity Title: Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3
  • Host Entity: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)
  • Assignment Country: Ethiopia
  • Modality: Online
  • Duration: 7 weeks
  • Time Commitment: 11–15 hours per week
  • Task Type: Development of plans
  • Relevant Sustainable Development Goal: SDG 17 – Partnerships for the Goals
  • Expected Start Date: The listing does not provide a valid start date
  • Number of Assignments: 0 as indicated in the provided listing
  • Language: English, fluent level desirable
  • Deadline: No application deadline is specified in the provided opportunity details

What Is Agenda 2063?

Agenda 2063 is Africa’s long-term development framework and vision for building “The Africa We Want.” It provides a continental framework for transforming Africa economically, socially and politically while promoting inclusive development, sustainable growth, integration and stronger partnerships.

However, understanding Agenda 2063 as a policy or development framework is only one part of the challenge. Its implementation also depends on the actions of individuals and institutions operating in different environments.

This is the central idea behind Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces.

The programme recognizes that important decisions are made every day in many different environments, including:

  • Governments and public institutions
  • Businesses and private-sector organizations
  • Universities and research institutions
  • Schools and educational organizations
  • Communities and civil society
  • Development organizations
  • Families
  • Professional networks
  • Entrepreneurship and innovation spaces
  • Youth organizations
  • Other environments where people make decisions and create value

These environments are described as “Power Spaces.”

The programme encourages participants to identify the Power Spaces available to them and consider how they can deliberately use those spaces to contribute to Africa’s long-term transformation.

What Is Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3?

Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3 is a seven-week online traineeship and volunteer learning experience designed to move participants beyond simply knowing about Agenda 2063.

The programme seeks to help participants answer an important question:

How can I personally contribute to achieving The Africa We Want through the spaces in which I have influence?

Rather than treating leadership as something limited to senior government officials, executives or institutional leaders, the programme takes a broader approach.

It recognizes that individuals can create value and influence outcomes from wherever they operate.

A student can influence a university or student organization. An entrepreneur can influence a business ecosystem. A teacher can influence learners and communities. A researcher can influence policy and knowledge. A community leader can influence local development. A communications professional can influence public awareness and engagement.

The programme therefore focuses on developing individual agency and helping participants recognize themselves as potential contributors to Agenda 2063.

Main Objective of the Programme

The central objective is to help participants progress from understanding Agenda 2063 to recognizing themselves as agents capable of contributing to its implementation.

The seven-week journey provides a structured framework through which participants examine:

  1. The value they currently create.
  2. The future they want to help create.
  3. The changes required to move from the present toward that future.
  4. The leadership values required to make meaningful decisions.
  5. The routines needed to turn intentions into action.
  6. The future they want to experience as a result of their efforts.
  7. The lessons they gain and the changes they need to make going forward.

This makes the programme particularly relevant to people interested in leadership, development practice, public policy, entrepreneurship, education, community development and African transformation.

The Seven Leadership Tools Participants Will Develop

One of the most important features of Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3 is its seven-tool leadership architecture.

Throughout the seven-week journey, participants progressively work with seven leadership tools.

1. Contribution Statement – What Value Do I Create?

The first tool encourages participants to identify their personal contribution to Africa’s transformation.

Participants examine their current Power Space and consider the value they create within it.

This may involve asking questions such as:

  • What am I currently contributing?
  • Who benefits from my contribution?
  • What capabilities do I possess?
  • What problems am I helping to solve?
  • Where do I have influence?
  • How does my work or activity connect with Africa’s broader development needs?

The Contribution Statement helps participants understand where they currently fit within the broader transformation agenda.

2. Moonshot – What Future Am I Committed to Creating?

The second tool focuses on developing a sufficiently ambitious vision for the future.

The concept of a “Moonshot” encourages participants to think beyond incremental improvements and identify a consequential future they are committed to helping create.

Participants consider:

  • What future do I want to see?
  • What would meaningful transformation look like?
  • What ambitious outcome would challenge current assumptions?
  • What future is worth working toward despite present obstacles?

The exercise is intended to help participants challenge the limitations imposed by present circumstances.

3. Delivery – What Must Change?

Having identified a desired future, participants then examine what needs to change to move toward it.

The Delivery tool focuses on the gap between the current situation and the desired outcome.

Participants may consider:

  • What is preventing progress?
  • Which systems, behaviours or practices need to change?
  • What obstacles must be addressed?
  • Which changes are most critical?
  • What actions can contribute to the desired transformation?

This stage helps translate vision into a practical understanding of what needs to happen.

4. Leadership Values – Who Must I Be?

The fourth tool focuses on the personal qualities and values required to pursue meaningful change.

Participants reflect on the type of leader they need to become in order to make consequential decisions and remain committed to their goals.

This can involve examining:

  • Personal values
  • Integrity
  • Responsibility
  • Courage
  • Accountability
  • Resilience
  • Collaboration
  • Commitment
  • Respect for others
  • Willingness to learn and adapt

The emphasis is not simply on what participants want to achieve but also on who they need to be throughout the journey.

5. Leadership Routines – What Must I Repeatedly Do?

A vision only becomes meaningful when it is translated into consistent action.

The Leadership Routines tool helps participants identify repeated behaviours and practices that can gradually produce results.

Participants consider:

  • What actions must I perform consistently?
  • Which habits will support my goals?
  • What behaviours need to become routine?
  • How can I turn intention into practice?
  • What repeated actions can accumulate into meaningful results?

This stage emphasizes the importance of sustained action rather than one-time motivation.

6. Letter from the Future – What Does Life Look Like Because I Succeeded?

The sixth tool asks participants to imagine their desired future as though they have already achieved it.

Through a Letter from the Future, participants explore what life looks like because their efforts succeeded.

This exercise can help participants:

  • Visualize the impact of their contribution.
  • Understand the consequences of achieving their goals.
  • Reconsider current choices.
  • Identify actions that are consistent with their desired future.
  • Strengthen their connection to their long-term objectives.

The exercise links future aspirations with present-day decision-making.

7. Future Review – What Have I Learned and What Should I Now Revise?

The final tool focuses on reflection, learning and continuous improvement.

Participants are introduced to the practice of:

Return → Review → Revise → Recommit

This process encourages participants to revisit their leadership plans and assess whether their circumstances, experiences and capabilities have changed.

Instead of treating the seven-week programme as an endpoint, participants are encouraged to continue applying the tools after the formal traineeship ends.

What Will Online Volunteers Do?

Online Volunteers will play a supporting role throughout the seven-week traineeship.

Their responsibilities will include the following.

Study the Learning Materials

Volunteers will become familiar with the Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces learning materials, including the Reader and associated resources.

This requires participants to:

  • Read the provided materials.
  • Understand the major concepts.
  • Engage critically with the learning content.
  • Prepare to support participant learning.
  • Develop familiarity with the seven leadership tools.

Volunteers are not expected to arrive as experts. The assignment specifically emphasizes curiosity and disciplined engagement with the materials.

Support Participant Engagement

Volunteers will help support participants throughout the seven-week learning journey.

This involves understanding the weekly concepts, questions and exercises and helping participants remain engaged with the programme.

The emphasis is on supporting learning rather than simply delivering course content.

Participate in Small-Group Learning Conversations

Where assigned, volunteers will participate in small-group conversations.

These discussions are intended to encourage participants to connect the leadership tools to their own Power Spaces.

Volunteers should therefore be capable of:

  • Listening actively.
  • Encouraging participation.
  • Asking constructive questions.
  • Helping participants connect concepts to their own experiences.
  • Providing concise and useful feedback.
  • Supporting a collaborative learning environment.

Contribute to the End-of-Cohort Review

Volunteers will also participate in a structured review at the end of the cohort.

They will help identify:

  • What worked well.
  • What challenges participants experienced.
  • What could be improved.
  • Which learning approaches were effective.
  • How future cohorts could be strengthened.
  • How the materials and participant experience could be improved.

This means volunteers can contribute not only to the current cohort but also to the continued development of the programme.

Who Can Apply?

The opportunity welcomes applications from people with an interest in Africa’s transformation and related areas.

The requirements specifically mention applicants from a variety of professional and educational backgrounds, including:

  • Professionals
  • Development practitioners
  • Researchers
  • Entrepreneurs
  • Educators
  • Students
  • Community leaders

Applicants may come from different sectors and Power Spaces.

The programme is therefore not restricted to one profession or academic discipline.

Required Experience and Skills

Candidates should be able to demonstrate a strong interest in one or more areas connected to Agenda 2063 and African development.

Relevant areas include:

  • Agenda 2063
  • African development
  • Leadership
  • Development practice
  • Public policy
  • Business
  • Education
  • Community development
  • Related fields

Applicants should also demonstrate the following capabilities.

Critical Reading and Learning

Candidates should be comfortable reading learning materials and engaging with them critically.

The programme requires volunteers to understand concepts sufficiently to support discussions and participant engagement.

Strong Written Communication

Good written communication is important because volunteers may need to provide feedback, participate in discussions and communicate ideas clearly.

Strong Interpersonal Communication

The role involves interaction with other participants, particularly through small-group learning conversations.

Applicants should therefore be comfortable communicating respectfully and constructively with people from different backgrounds.

Constructive Feedback

Volunteers should be able to provide feedback that is:

  • Concise
  • Clear
  • Constructive
  • Relevant
  • Helpful to the learning process

Commitment

Applicants must be able to commit to the assignment throughout the seven-week Cohort 3 period.

The expected workload is 11–15 hours per week, making it important for applicants to assess their availability before applying.

Language Requirement

The listed language requirement is:

English – Fluent, desirable.

Applicants should therefore be able to comfortably understand and engage with English-language learning materials and participate effectively in written and interpersonal communication.

Programme Modality and Time Commitment

The assignment is conducted entirely online.

This makes it suitable for participants who can contribute remotely without needing to relocate to Ethiopia or another physical programme location.

The expected commitment is:

11–15 hours per week for seven weeks.

Applicants should ensure they have sufficient time to:

  • Study the learning materials.
  • Participate in learning conversations.
  • Support participant engagement.
  • Complete assigned activities.
  • Contribute to the end-of-cohort review.

What Makes This Opportunity Different?

One of the distinctive features of the programme is that it does not simply present Agenda 2063 as something participants should know.

Instead, it asks participants to consider how they can personally contribute to its implementation.

This approach is important because continental transformation depends not only on governments and large institutions but also on the decisions and actions taken in everyday environments.

The programme’s Power Spaces approach recognizes that individuals have different forms of influence.

A participant does not necessarily need to occupy a senior position to contribute to development.

Their influence could come through:

  • Their profession
  • Their organization
  • Their business
  • Their research
  • Their classroom
  • Their community
  • Their professional network
  • Their family
  • Their youth or civic activities
  • Their educational institution

This makes the programme relevant to participants at different stages of their careers and lives.

Leadership Portfolio and Letter from the Future

Participants are expected to retain important outputs from the learning journey, including their Leadership Portfolio and Letter from the Future.

These materials can serve as practical references after the seven-week programme.

Rather than treating leadership development as a one-time training activity, the programme encourages participants to revisit their materials periodically as their circumstances, experience, capabilities and Power Spaces evolve.

This creates an opportunity for continuous reflection and development.

Contribution to Future Cohorts

Another important aspect of Cohort 3 is its contribution to the continued improvement of the programme.

Participants and volunteers will help test and improve:

  • Learning materials
  • Facilitation approaches
  • Participant engagement methods
  • Overall learning experience
  • Approaches for making the leadership practice accessible to larger numbers of people

Consequently, participation can contribute to the development of future iterations of Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces.

Connection to Sustainable Development Goal 17

The assignment is linked to Sustainable Development Goal 17: Partnerships for the Goals.

SDG 17 emphasizes the importance of partnerships in achieving sustainable development.

The connection is particularly relevant because Agenda 2063 implementation requires collaboration among governments, businesses, communities, civil society, educational institutions, development organizations and individuals.

By encouraging people to identify their Power Spaces and collaborate across different environments, the programme reinforces the importance of partnerships in achieving long-term development objectives.

Is This a Paid Opportunity?

The provided description identifies this as an online volunteer assignment.

It specifically explains that volunteerism involves activities undertaken freely for the public good where monetary reward is not the principal motivating factor.

Therefore, applicants should not approach this as a paid employment opportunity.

The programme is better suited to individuals interested in learning, leadership development, contribution to African development, collaboration and volunteer experience.

Inclusivity and Equal Opportunity

The programme states that United Nations Volunteers is an equal opportunity programme that welcomes qualified applicants.

It is committed to diversity and respect for human rights and individual dignity.

The inclusivity statement specifies that discrimination should not occur on the basis of characteristics including:

  • Race
  • Sex
  • Gender identity
  • Religion
  • Nationality
  • Ethnic origin
  • Sexual orientation
  • Disability
  • Pregnancy
  • Age
  • Language
  • Social origin
  • Other status

The programme therefore emphasizes an inclusive environment in which qualified individuals from diverse backgrounds can participate.

Who Is the Ideal Candidate?

The ideal candidate is someone who is genuinely interested in contributing to Africa’s long-term development and is willing to learn rather than simply demonstrate existing expertise.

A strong applicant could be someone who:

  1. Has an interest in Agenda 2063 and African development.
  2. Is passionate about leadership and positive change.
  3. Can critically read and understand learning materials.
  4. Communicates clearly in English.
  5. Works effectively with other people.
  6. Can provide constructive feedback.
  7. Is comfortable participating in online learning.
  8. Can dedicate 11–15 hours every week for seven weeks.
  9. Is open to learning from people with different experiences.
  10. Can connect abstract ideas with real-world contexts.
  11. Is willing to reflect on their own contribution and leadership.
  12. Wants to continue applying the programme’s tools beyond the formal traineeship.

Benefits of Participating

Although the opportunity is a volunteer assignment rather than a paid position, participants can gain several forms of professional and personal value.

Leadership Development

The seven-tool framework provides participants with a structured approach to examining their contribution, aspirations, values, routines and future goals.

Understanding of Agenda 2063

Participants gain an opportunity to engage directly with Agenda 2063 and explore its relevance to individual action and African transformation.

Practical Reflection

The programme goes beyond theoretical learning by encouraging participants to apply the concepts to their own Power Spaces.

Collaboration

Small-group learning conversations provide opportunities to engage with people from different professional, educational and community backgrounds.

Communication Skills

Supporting discussions and providing constructive feedback can strengthen written and interpersonal communication.

Development Perspective

The programme can help participants connect individual leadership with broader development objectives.

International Volunteer Experience

Participation in an online UN-linked volunteer assignment can provide experience of contributing to an international development-oriented initiative.

How to Prepare for the Opportunity

Applicants interested in this programme should carefully consider how their existing experience connects with the assignment.

Before applying, it can be useful to reflect on the following questions:

  • What does Agenda 2063 mean to me?
  • What aspect of African development interests me most?
  • What Power Space do I currently operate in?
  • What value do I create in that space?
  • What development challenge would I like to help address?
  • What leadership qualities do I already demonstrate?
  • What leadership qualities do I need to strengthen?
  • Can I dedicate 11–15 hours per week for seven weeks?
  • Can I effectively communicate and collaborate with people online?
  • How could my professional, academic, entrepreneurial or community experience contribute to the programme?

Applicants should also ensure that their application clearly demonstrates their motivation, relevant interests, communication abilities and commitment.

Important Scam Warning

Applicants should be particularly careful about fraudulent individuals or websites claiming to represent the United Nations.

The opportunity information explicitly warns that the United Nations does not charge application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or recruitment fees.

If anyone requests money in exchange for applying, being shortlisted, receiving training or securing recruitment, applicants should disregard the request.

Applicants should also exercise caution when submitting personal information online because logos, names, addresses and other organizational materials can be copied and reproduced by scammers.

Always verify that an application is being submitted through the legitimate United Nations or UN Volunteers recruitment platform.

Application Deadline

No application deadline is specified in the opportunity information provided.

Applicants should therefore check the official listing for the current application status and any deadline or closing date before submitting an application.

The provided listing also shows an invalid/unspecified expected start date, so applicants should verify the latest programme schedule through the official recruitment platform.

APPLY HERE

Conclusion

The Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3 provides an opportunity to engage with Africa’s long-term development vision from a personal and practical leadership perspective.

Its central message is that achieving The Africa We Want is not solely the responsibility of governments or major institutions. Transformation can also emerge from the many Power Spaces in which individuals learn, work, build businesses, conduct research, educate others, participate in communities and make decisions.

Over seven weeks, participants will explore seven practical leadership tools covering contribution, vision, delivery, values, routines, future thinking and continuous review. They will also support other learners, participate in group conversations and contribute feedback that can improve future cohorts.

For professionals, students, researchers, entrepreneurs, educators, practitioners and community leaders interested in Africa’s development, this online volunteer assignment can provide a structured opportunity to deepen their understanding of Agenda 2063 while reflecting on how their own work and influence can contribute to the continent’s transformation.

With a commitment of 11–15 hours per week for seven weeks, applicants should ensure that they have sufficient time and motivation to participate fully. Most importantly, successful participation requires more than familiarity with development terminology. It requires curiosity, critical thinking, communication, collaboration and a genuine willingness to connect ideas with action.

The programme ultimately encourages participants to move from asking “What is Agenda 2063?” toward a more personal and consequential question: “What can I contribute to achieving The Africa We Want through the Power Spaces available to me?”
