item.content:encoded:
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is offering a research and training opportunity through the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE) for qualified researchers and graduate-level professionals interested in physical activity promotion, public health, community design, implementation science, epidemiology, data analysis, policy, and related fields.

The CDC Advancing Active People, Healthy Nation Through Science – Physical Activity Fellowship, referenced as CDC-2026-0033, provides an opportunity for an eligible participant to train with CDC’s National Center for Chronic Disease Prevention and Health Promotion (NCCDPHP), specifically within the Division of Nutrition, Physical Activity, and Obesity (DNPAO) in Atlanta, Georgia.

This fellowship is particularly relevant to individuals interested in using scientific research, data, policy, community partnerships, and evidence-based interventions to increase physical activity and improve public health outcomes.

About the CDC Physical Activty Fellowship

The fellowship is connected to Active People, Healthy Nation, a national CDC initiative designed to help 27 million Americans become more physically active by 2027.

The initiative recognizes physical activity as an important component of population health and seeks to create environments and systems that make physical activity easier and more accessible.

As an ORISE participant, the selected fellow will work alongside multidisciplinary teams at CDC and the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS). The training experience will involve research, evidence translation, partnership development, communication, evaluation, policy analysis, and dissemination activities related to physical activity promotion.

A major area of focus is activity-friendly community design. This involves identifying, evaluating, and communicating evidence-based approaches that increase opportunities for people to:

  • Walk
  • Bicycle
  • Use public transportation
  • Access everyday destinations through active transportation
  • Engage in other forms of routine physical activity

The fellowship therefore goes beyond traditional exercise promotion. It examines how communities, transportation systems, policies, urban environments, and public health strategies can be designed to support healthier and more physically active populations.

Research Project

The selected ORISE participant will be placed within CDC’s National Center for Chronic Disease Prevention and Health Promotion, in the Division of Nutrition, Physical Activity, and Obesity.

The research and training experience will contribute to nationally significant public health initiatives that aim to generate, interpret, translate, and communicate scientific evidence.

The fellow will contribute to efforts supporting Active People, Healthy Nation and may participate in activities involving:

  1. Scientific research
  2. Evidence reviews
  3. Implementation science
  4. Evaluation
  5. Policy analysis
  6. Data analysis
  7. Community-level strategies
  8. Evidence translation
  9. Scientific writing
  10. Dissemination
  11. Partnership development
  12. Public health communication

The fellow will also have opportunities to work with experts and organizations across several disciplines, creating an interdisciplinary training environment.

Key Learning Objectives

One of the strongest features of this fellowship is the breadth of professional and research skills participants can develop.

Under the supervision and guidance of experienced mentors, the selected fellow will have opportunities to develop the following competencies.

1. Scientific Evidence Reviews

The participant will learn how to support scientific evidence reviews, coordination, and communication activities that may contribute to future updates of the Physical Activity Guidelines for Americans, 2nd Edition.

This experience can provide valuable exposure to the process of reviewing scientific evidence and translating research findings into public health guidance.

2. National Partnership Development

The fellow will learn how to engage with national partners in support of updates to the National Physical Activity Plan.

This can involve working with organizations and stakeholders whose activities influence physical activity, health promotion, community development, transportation, and related areas.

3. Scientific Writing and Publications

The fellowship provides opportunities to develop experience in authoring or co-authoring:

  • Peer-reviewed scientific manuscripts
  • Scientific reports
  • Conference presentations
  • Evidence summaries
  • Other scientific communication products

This is particularly valuable for candidates interested in establishing or strengthening a research and academic career.

4. Implementation Science

Participants will build knowledge and skills in implementation science, which focuses on understanding how evidence-based interventions, programs, and policies can be effectively translated into real-world practice.

This may include examining why certain interventions work in particular communities and how successful strategies can be implemented or scaled.

5. Evaluation and Dissemination Research

The fellow will have opportunities to gain experience in evaluation and dissemination research.

These skills are important in determining whether public health programs and strategies are achieving their intended objectives and how evidence can be effectively communicated to organizations, policymakers, professionals, and communities.

6. Policy Analysis

The fellowship includes opportunities to understand policy analysis and evaluation related to community design and physical activity promotion.

This can involve examining how policies and community-level decisions influence opportunities for physical activity.

7. Quantitative and Qualitative Analysis

Participants will learn to apply both quantitative and qualitative analytical methods.

Depending on project needs, this may include working with:

  • Statistical data
  • Qualitative data
  • Mixed-method approaches
  • R
  • Python
  • GIS
  • Spatial analysis
  • Emerging analytical approaches

Candidates with existing data-analysis experience may therefore find this opportunity particularly relevant.

8. Interdisciplinary Collaboration

The fellow will work in interdisciplinary groups and interact with professionals from fields such as:

  • Public health
  • Physical activity
  • Tribal health
  • Urban planning
  • Epidemiology
  • Community planning
  • Transportation planning
  • Policy
  • Research

This provides an opportunity to understand public health problems from multiple professional perspectives.

9. Qualitative Research

The participant will build skills in qualitative methodology, including opportunities related to qualitative data collection, methodology, and analysis.

10. Data Analysis and Evidence Translation

The fellowship will provide opportunities to analyze data and translate scientific findings into products that can be understood and used by different audiences.

Participants may contribute to manuscripts and other materials addressing physical activity and community-level interventions.

11. Public Health Communication

The fellow will gain experience developing materials such as:

  • Infographics
  • Fact sheets
  • Evidence summaries
  • Messaging materials
  • Other communication products

These materials may be designed for policymakers, public health professionals, leadership, professionals in other sectors, and the general public.

12. Presentation Skills

Participants will also develop their ability to prepare and deliver presentations to internal and external audiences.

This can strengthen communication skills that are essential for researchers and public health professionals.

Preferred Skills and Experience

Although the opportunity has specific eligibility requirements, CDC has also identified several preferred skills that can strengthen an applicant’s profile.

The preferred candidate may have experience in:

  • Strong oral and written communication
  • Scientific writing
  • Peer-reviewed publications
  • Scientific reports
  • Scientific communication
  • Teamwork
  • Partner engagement
  • Physical activity
  • Active transportation
  • Land-use planning
  • Parks and recreation
  • Related public health sectors
  • Qualitative data
  • Qualitative research methodology
  • Qualitative data analysis
  • Translating scientific findings into plain language
  • R
  • Python
  • Tribal organizations and communities
  • Implementation science
  • Evaluation methods
  • Mixed-methods research
  • GIS/spatial analysis
  • Community planning
  • Transportation planning
  • Data visualization

Applicants do not necessarily need to possess every preferred skill. The fellowship is designed as a training experience, and candidates should highlight the relevant skills and experiences they already possess.

Who Is Eligible to Apply?

The opportunity has a specific eligibility requirement that applicants should carefully review before beginning an application.

Citizenship Requirement

The fellowship is available to U.S. citizens only.

This means that individuals who are citizens of other countries but do not hold U.S. citizenship are not eligible for this particular opportunity.

There is no race or ethnicity restriction stated in the eligibility requirements. However, the citizenship requirement is mandatory.

Academic Requirement

Applicants must have:

  • A master’s degree, or
  • A doctoral degree

in one of the eligible disciplines.

The degree must have been received within the previous 60 months.

Alternatively, applicants who are currently pursuing a qualifying master’s or doctoral degree may be eligible if they anticipate graduating by January 27, 2027.

Eligible Academic Disciplines

The listed eligible disciplines fall into two broad categories:

Life, Health and Medical Sciences

Applicants with relevant academic backgrounds within the life, health, and medical sciences may qualify, depending on how their degree aligns with the fellowship’s requirements.

Social and Behavioral Sciences

Applicants from relevant social and behavioral science disciplines may also qualify.

Because the fellowship focuses on physical activity, public health, community design, policy, implementation, evaluation, and behavioral and population-level interventions, candidates should carefully demonstrate how their academic background connects with the fellowship’s research objectives.

Where Is the Fellowship Located?

The research opportunity is based at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention in Atlanta, Georgia, USA.

The fellow will participate in a full-time training appointment and work with CDC and HHS teams involved in physical activity and public health initiatives.

Fellowship Duration

The appointment is initially expected to last one year.

However, the appointment may be renewed upon the recommendation of CDC and depending on the availability of funding.

The anticipated start date is listed as September 31, 2026, although the opportunity states that the start date is flexible and will depend on several factors.

Applicants should note that September has only 30 days. Therefore, the stated September 31 date appears to be a date-entry inconsistency in the announcement, and applicants should rely on the official application information or contact the listed point of contact if the exact start date is important to their application.

Learn More About This Opportunity HERE

Level of Participation

This is a full-time appointment.

The selected participant will therefore be expected to devote full-time participation to the fellowship and its research and training activities.

Participant Stipend

The fellowship provides a participant stipend.

However, the announcement does not provide one fixed stipend amount.

The stipend rate may vary according to several factors, including:

  • The specific opportunity
  • Location
  • Educational background
  • Experience
  • Other applicable factors

Candidates who reach the interview stage may ask about the exact stipend rate.

If selected, the official appointment offer will state the applicable monthly stipend.

Applicants should therefore avoid assuming a specific dollar amount unless it is provided directly by ORISE or in their appointment offer.

Health Insurance and Participant Status

ORISE participants do not become employees of CDC, the U.S. Department of Energy, or ORAU.

The fellowship also does not provide traditional employment-related benefits associated with being a CDC employee.

Proof of health insurance is required for participation.

Health insurance may be obtained through ORISE.

Prospective applicants should therefore understand that this is a structured research and training appointment rather than a standard CDC employment position.

Environmental, Safety and Health Requirements

Successful applicants will be required to comply with the environmental, safety, and health requirements applicable to the hosting facility.

These requirements may include health and safety measures established by the facility, including applicable COVID-19-related requirements such as:

  • Facial covering
  • Physical distancing
  • Testing
  • Vaccination

Applicants should be prepared to comply with the requirements applicable at the time of their appointment.

How to Apply

A complete application must contain all required components.

Applicants should prepare the following:

1. Application Form

Complete and submit the official application through the designated ORISE application system.

Apply HERE

2. Academic Transcripts

Applicants must provide the required transcripts.

The announcement specifies that applicants should review the detailed ORISE transcript guidelines to determine what constitutes an acceptable transcript.

If documents are not in English, an official English translation must be included.

3. Current Resume or CV

The resume/CV should be current and should clearly present relevant academic and professional experience.

It should include information such as:

  • Academic history
  • Employment history
  • Relevant research or professional experience
  • Publications, where applicable
  • Relevant technical skills
  • Other experiences related to the fellowship

Candidates should tailor their CV to the research focus rather than submitting a generic resume whenever possible.

4. Recommendation

Applicants must provide one educational or professional recommendation.

This is an important requirement.

The application will be considered incomplete and will not be reviewed until at least one recommendation has been submitted.

Applicants should therefore contact their recommender early enough to ensure the recommendation is submitted before the application is reviewed.

Language Requirement

All application documents must be submitted in English.

If an applicant’s documents are in another language, they must include an official English translation.

This requirement applies particularly to academic documents and other materials submitted as part of the application.

Application Deadline

The application deadline is:

September 11, 2026, at 3:00 PM Eastern Time.

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.

Because applications may be reviewed before the final deadline, applicants should not wait until September 11 to submit their materials.

A strong strategy is to prepare the CV, transcripts, recommendation, and other application materials well in advance and submit a complete application as early as possible..

Why This Fellowship Could Be Valuable

This opportunity offers more than a traditional academic research placement.

A successful participant could gain exposure to the way a major U.S. public health agency uses research evidence to influence programs, policies, community strategies, and public health communication.

Some of the major professional development areas include:

  • Public health research
  • Scientific writing
  • Evidence synthesis
  • Policy analysis
  • Implementation science
  • Evaluation
  • Data analysis
  • Qualitative research
  • GIS and spatial analysis
  • Scientific communication
  • Public health messaging
  • Community design
  • Active transportation
  • Partnership development
  • Interdisciplinary collaboration
  • Conference presentations
  • Peer-reviewed publications

For researchers interested in population health and physical activity, the fellowship could provide an opportunity to work at the intersection of science, policy, community planning, and public health practice.

Who Should Consider Applying?

This fellowship may be particularly suitable for eligible U.S. citizens who are pursuing or have recently completed graduate-level education in areas connected to health, medicine, life sciences, social sciences, behavioral sciences, public health, epidemiology, or related disciplines.

Candidates with experience in any of the following areas may find the opportunity especially relevant:

  • Public health
  • Epidemiology
  • Physical activity research
  • Health promotion
  • Behavioral science
  • Community health
  • Implementation science
  • Program evaluation
  • Qualitative research
  • Quantitative research
  • Mixed-methods research
  • Urban planning
  • Transportation planning
  • GIS
  • Data science
  • Policy analysis
  • Health communication
  • Scientific writing

The strongest applicants should demonstrate not only academic qualifications but also an ability to work collaboratively, communicate scientific findings, analyze information, and connect research evidence with real-world public health practice.

Application Preparation Tips

Before submitting an application, prospective applicants should carefully check that their materials demonstrate a clear connection between their background and the fellowship.

Tailor your CV

Emphasize research, publications, data analysis, public health projects, community work, presentations, and other experiences relevant to the fellowship.

Demonstrate research skills

If you have experience with R, Python, GIS, qualitative research, quantitative analysis, mixed methods, or data visualization, make those skills easy for reviewers to identify.

Highlight scientific communication

Publications, research reports, conference presentations, policy briefs, infographics, fact sheets, and other communication products can demonstrate your ability to translate evidence for different audiences.

Connect your experience to physical activity

Experience involving physical activity, active transportation, community planning, parks, land use, health promotion, or related sectors can be particularly valuable.

Secure your recommendation early

Because the application will not be reviewed until a recommendation has been submitted, applicants should not leave this requirement until the last minute.

Apply early

The opportunity uses rolling review. Submitting a complete application early may therefore be preferable to waiting until the final deadline.

CONCLUSION

The CDC Advancing Active People, Healthy Nation Through Science – Physical Activity Fellowship is a specialized research and training opportunity for eligible U.S. citizens with a recent or forthcoming master’s or doctoral degree in a relevant discipline.

The fellowship combines public health research, physical activity promotion, community design, policy analysis, implementation science, evaluation, data analysis, scientific writing, and evidence translation. Participants will have the opportunity to work with multidisciplinary professionals while contributing to initiatives connected to CDC’s Active People, Healthy Nation campaign.

With a full-time initial appointment of one year, a participant stipend, opportunities for professional development, and potential exposure to peer-reviewed research and national public health initiatives, the fellowship can be particularly valuable for graduate-level researchers seeking experience in applied public health science.

However, applicants should pay close attention to the eligibility requirements. The opportunity is restricted to U.S. citizens, requires a qualifying master’s or doctoral degree obtained within the past 60 months or anticipated by January 27, 2027, and requires a complete application containing the application form, transcripts, current CV/resume, and at least one educational or professional recommendation.

Most importantly, applicants should remember the September 11, 2026, 3:00 PM Eastern Time deadline and the fact that applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. Preparing and submitting a complete, carefully tailored application early can help ensure that the application is available for consideration.

item.content:encoded:
The African Nutrition Leadership Programme (ANLP) is a leadership development initiative focused on strengthening nutrition leadership capacity across the African continent. Based at North-West University in South Africa, the programme works to develop the leadership abilities of early- and mid-career nutrition professionals and other stakeholders whose work contributes to improving nutrition and health outcomes in Africa. The ANLP has been successfully delivering its flagship 10-day Leadership Development Programme since 2002, bringing together professionals from a broad range of nutrition-related disciplines and sectors. Through an intensive leadership development experience, the programme aims to equip participants with the knowledge, skills, perspectives and leadership capabilities needed to contribute more effectively to nutrition programmes, policies, institutions and initiatives across Africa. Applications and further information are available for the 2027 ANLP programme.

About the African Nutrition Leadership Programme

The African Nutrition Leadership Programme was established around the goal of developing both individual and institutional leadership capacity in nutrition at different levels across Africa.

Nutrition challenges on the continent are complex and often require collaboration between professionals working in health, agriculture, education, policy, research, community development, government, international organisations and other sectors. Effective leadership is therefore an important part of developing and implementing sustainable nutrition solutions.

The ANLP seeks to respond to this need by providing leadership development opportunities for professionals who are already working in, or are closely connected to, the nutrition sector.

The programme is based at North-West University in South Africa and has a particular commitment to developing the leadership potential of early- and mid-career professionals.

What Is the ANLP 10-Day Leadership Development Programme?

The flagship ANLP programme is an intensive 10-day leadership development programme for individuals.

Since 2002, the programme has brought together participants from a wide variety of nutrition-related backgrounds. Rather than focusing exclusively on one profession or sector, the ANLP welcomes a multidisciplinary approach to nutrition leadership.

This creates an environment where participants can engage with people who approach nutrition challenges from different professional and institutional perspectives.

The programme is intended to strengthen participants’ leadership capacity so they can become more effective contributors within their organisations, professional networks and the wider nutrition community.

Who Participates in the African Nutrition Leadership Programme?

One of the notable features of the ANLP is the diversity of professional backgrounds represented among its participants.

According to the programme description, previous participants have come from a wide range of nutrition-related disciplines and sectors, including:

  • Government institutions
  • United Nations organisations
  • Civil society organisations
  • Academic institutions
  • The private sector
  • Individual consultants
  • Other nutrition-related professional fields and stakeholder groups

This multidisciplinary participation is important because nutrition is influenced by many interconnected areas, including health, food systems, agriculture, public policy, education, research and community development.

By bringing professionals from different sectors together, the programme provides an opportunity for participants to learn from different experiences and perspectives while developing their own leadership approaches.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The ANLP is particularly relevant to early- and mid-career nutrition professionals and related stakeholders working in Africa.

Potential applicants may include professionals whose work, research, programmes or institutional responsibilities are connected to nutrition or related areas.

The programme may be particularly valuable for individuals who:

  • Work in nutrition-related roles within government.
  • Work with United Nations agencies or other international organisations.
  • Work for civil society or non-governmental organisations involved in nutrition.
  • Are involved in nutrition-related academic or research activities.
  • Work in the private sector in areas connected to nutrition.
  • Work as independent consultants in nutrition or related fields.
  • Have responsibilities that require them to influence nutrition policies, programmes or initiatives.
  • Are developing their leadership capabilities as early- or mid-career professionals.
  • Want to strengthen their ability to lead, collaborate and contribute to nutrition-related initiatives across Africa.

Applicants should consult the official 2027 application information to confirm the specific eligibility and selection requirements applicable to the upcoming programme.

African Focus of the Programme

The African Nutrition Leadership Programme has a continent-wide focus.

Its purpose is not simply to develop individual professional skills but to contribute to broader leadership capacity within the African nutrition community.

The programme recognises that African countries face diverse nutrition challenges and that effective solutions require leadership that is responsive to local and regional realities.

By developing professionals from different African countries and professional environments, the ANLP contributes to a wider network of nutrition leaders who can apply their learning within their own organisations and communities.

Individual and Institutional Leadership Development

A key aspect of the ANLP is its focus on leadership at both the individual and institutional levels.

Individual leadership development can help professionals become more effective in their roles, communicate more effectively, work across professional boundaries and take greater responsibility for initiatives within their organisations.

At the institutional level, stronger leadership can help organisations improve how they plan, coordinate and implement nutrition-related activities.

The ANLP therefore goes beyond the idea of leadership as simply managing people. Its broader objective is to strengthen leadership capacity that can contribute to improved nutrition action across different levels of the African nutrition sector.

Tailor-Made Leadership and Functional Capacity Development

In addition to the 10-day programme for individual participants, the ANLP also offers tailor-made leadership and functional capacity development programmes.

These programmes are designed around the needs of particular stakeholders or institutions.

This means that the ANLP’s work extends beyond an individual training model. Organisations and stakeholders can potentially engage with the programme to address specific leadership and functional capacity development needs within their institutions.

The tailor-made approach allows capacity development to be connected more closely to an organisation’s particular circumstances, priorities and requirements.

Why Leadership Matters in Nutrition

Nutrition is a multidisciplinary field, and addressing nutrition challenges often requires cooperation among many different actors.

A nutrition professional may need to work with government officials, researchers, community organisations, international agencies, healthcare professionals, businesses and other stakeholders.

Leadership skills can therefore be important for:

  • Building effective partnerships.
  • Coordinating people and institutions.
  • Communicating ideas and priorities.
  • Influencing decision-making.
  • Managing complex programmes.
  • Supporting collaboration across sectors.
  • Responding to changing nutrition challenges.
  • Strengthening organisational capacity.
  • Contributing to evidence-informed policy and programmes.

The ANLP’s leadership-focused approach is intended to help professionals become better equipped to operate within this complex environment.

What Makes the ANLP Significant?

The programme has a substantial history of delivering leadership development opportunities for nutrition professionals.

The 10-day individual programme has been successfully hosted since 2002, meaning that the initiative has a long-standing presence in African nutrition leadership development.

Its multidisciplinary participant base is another important feature. Participants have historically represented government, the UN, civil society, academia, the private sector and consultancy.

This broad professional representation creates the potential for participants to gain perspectives beyond their immediate professional environments.

Application for the ANLP 2027 Programme

Individuals interested in participating in the 2027 African Nutrition Leadership Programme can access the application form provided by the programme.

Applicants should carefully review the application requirements and provide the requested information when completing the form.

Application form:https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSccz7d63XVN2kXuHUoQuni6BHt5ndsQA6CARnga0TAmgAoJtQ/viewform
because the supplied announcement does not provide a specific closing date, prospective applicants should consult the application form and official ANLP information for the 2027 application deadline and any updated eligibility requirements.

Important Information for Prospective Applicants

Before applying, prospective participants should consider the following:

  1. Professional background: The programme is focused on nutrition professionals and related stakeholders, particularly those at the early- and mid-career stages.
  2. African connection: The ANLP is designed around developing nutrition leadership capacity across the African continent.
  3. Multidisciplinary participation: Previous participants have represented government, the UN, civil society, academia, the private sector and consultancy.
  4. Leadership focus: The programme is specifically concerned with leadership development rather than being solely a technical nutrition course.
  5. Programme duration: The flagship individual programme lasts 10 days.
  6. 2027 application: Individuals interested in participating in the 2027 programme should use the provided application form and verify all current requirements before submitting their application.
  7. Deadline: No application deadline is stated in the information provided. Applicants should therefore check the current application materials for the official closing date.

Learn more here,https://africanutritionleadership.org/

Conclusion

The African Nutrition Leadership Programme (ANLP) provides an opportunity for nutrition professionals and related stakeholders across Africa to strengthen their leadership capacity and contribute more effectively to the development of nutrition initiatives on the continent. Based at North-West University in South Africa, the ANLP has been developing individual leadership capacity through its 10-day programme since 2002. Its participants have come from diverse professional environments, including government, the United Nations, civil society, academia, the private sector and consultancy. For early- and mid-career professionals seeking to strengthen their leadership abilities while engaging with a multidisciplinary African nutrition community, the 2027 ANLP programme represents an opportunity worth exploring.

Interested applicants should review the application form carefully, confirm their eligibility, check the official deadline and submit their application through the designated application process.

item.content:encoded:
The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is inviting applications for its Early Warning & Preparedness Internship 2026, a six-month, home-based internship supporting the organisation’s Disaster Risk Reduction and Recovery Team (DRT).

This opportunity is particularly relevant for students and recent graduates interested in disaster risk reduction, climate change adaptation, disaster management, humanitarian affairs, risk intelligence, artificial intelligence, digital technologies, early warning systems, and resilience building.

The internship will provide an opportunity to contribute to UNDP’s work on risk intelligence, preparedness, anticipation, and the use of digital and AI-powered technologies for disaster risk reduction. The successful intern will also support research, knowledge management, learning, and communications activities within the UNDP Crisis Bureau.

UNDP Early Warning & Preparedness Internship 2026 at a Glance

  • Organisation: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)
  • Position: Early Warning & Preparedness Intern
  • Job Identification: 35990
  • Location: Home-Based
  • Contract Duration: 6 months
  • Job Type: Full-time internship
  • Practice Area: Disaster Risk Reduction and Recovery
  • Grade: IN
  • Application Deadline: 1 September 2026 at 4:45 PM
  • Working Language: English
  • Other UN Languages: Knowledge of another UN official language is an asset.

About the UNDP Early Warning & Preparedness Internship

UNDP works with governments and partners at international, national, and local levels to reduce disaster risks, strengthen resilience, and promote development that is risk-informed and sustainable.

The Early Warning & Preparedness Internship forms part of this broader effort. The intern will contribute to activities involving risk intelligence, early warning, preparedness, anticipation, digital innovation, and artificial intelligence applications for disaster risk reduction.

The role combines research, analysis, technology, knowledge management, learning, and communications. This makes it particularly suitable for candidates who want to understand how emerging technologies and evidence-based approaches can be applied to real-world disaster and development challenges.

What Will the UNDP Intern Do?

The selected intern will support several areas of the Disaster Risk Reduction and Recovery Team’s work.

1. Risk Intelligence and Digital Innovation

A major component of the internship involves researching emerging developments in risk intelligence and digital technologies.

The intern may be expected to:

  • Conduct research and analysis on emerging trends, methodologies, tools, and best practices in risk intelligence and disaster risk reduction.
  • Explore developments in artificial intelligence, geospatial technologies, digital public infrastructure, and data ecosystems relevant to disaster risk reduction.
  • Support the continued development of UNDP’s Risk Intelligence Service Line.
  • Identify innovative approaches and document lessons learned.
  • Contribute to the development of service packages and value propositions.
  • Map and analyse AI-powered and digital applications relevant to risk intelligence.
  • Research technologies such as machine learning, predictive analytics, digital twins, remote sensing, geospatial intelligence, risk modelling, early warning systems, and data visualisation.
  • Develop knowledge products, concept notes, guidance materials, case studies, policy briefs, and communications products.
  • Identify opportunities for applying innovative digital technologies within UNDP programming.

This aspect of the internship is particularly valuable for applicants interested in the intersection of AI, data, technology, disaster preparedness, and international development.

2. Knowledge Sharing and Country-Level Good Practices

The intern will also help identify and communicate successful approaches being implemented by UNDP Country Offices, Regional Hubs and partners.

Responsibilities may include:

  • Documenting country-level good practices.
  • Identifying innovative solutions in disaster risk reduction and preparedness.
  • Supporting dissemination of lessons and experiences.
  • Engaging with technical institutions, research organisations, technology providers, UN entities, and academic institutions.
  • Contributing to presentations and briefing notes.
  • Supporting donor materials and proposals.
  • Contributing to strategic documents related to partnerships and resource mobilisation.

Through these activities, the intern can gain exposure to how international development organisations collect, package, and communicate knowledge to governments, partners, donors, and other stakeholders.

3. Preparedness Learning Pathway

Another important part of the internship is supporting the continued development of UNDP’s Preparedness Learning Pathway.

The intern will assist with:

  • Researching and categorising resources for the expansion and tailoring of the corporate learning package.
  • Supporting the development and maintenance of the online Preparedness Learning Pathway repository.
  • Contributing to a self-paced course under the UNDP Crisis Academy.
  • Researching resources for new thematic modules of the UNDP Preparedness Toolkit.

This provides exposure to learning and knowledge-management processes within a major international development organisation.

4. Webinars, Learning Activities, and Digital Engagement

The intern will also support webinars and related learning activities.

Tasks may include:

  • Preparing webinar plans.
  • Developing facilitation guidance.
  • Supporting MURAL boards.
  • Assisting with group discussions.
  • Supporting Zoom arrangements.
  • Preparing webinar reports.
  • Supporting other learning activities.
  • Contributing to serious game methodologies under the Preparedness Learning Pathway.
  • Developing social media kits for workshops and webinars.
  • Preparing presentations, talking points, and briefing notes relating to UNDP’s global early warning portfolio.

Candidates with strong communication, digital collaboration, and content-development skills may therefore find this component especially relevant.

5. Research, Analysis, and Communications

The internship also offers exposure to broader research and communications activities within the Disaster Risk Reduction and Recovery Team.

The intern may contribute to research and analysis concerning:

  • Urban resilience.
  • Gender equality and women’s leadership in disaster risk reduction.
  • Disaster risk financing.
  • Funding and project proposals.
  • Briefs and talking points.
  • Presentations and slide decks.
  • Knowledge management.
  • Communications activities.
  • Other research and analytical assignments as required.

Who Can Apply for the UNDP Internship?

Educational Qualifications

Applicants must meet at least one of the specified educational requirements at the time of application.

Eligible applicants include those who:

  1. Are enrolled in a postgraduate degree programme, such as a Master’s degree or higher, in:
    • Disaster risk reduction;
    • Climate change adaptation;
    • Disaster management; or
    • Humanitarian affairs.
  2. Are enrolled in the final academic year of a first university degree, such as a Bachelor’s degree or equivalent, in one of the relevant fields.
  3. Have recently graduated with a relevant university degree and, if selected, are able to begin the internship within one year of graduation.
  4. Are enrolled in a postgraduate professional traineeship programme and will undertake the internship as part of that programme.

Required Skills and Experience

Beyond academic qualifications, applicants should demonstrate a combination of communication, research, technology, and organisational skills.

Important capabilities include:

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to write clearly and concisely.
  • Good command of information and communication technology.
  • Strong research and analytical abilities.
  • Strong organisational skills.
  • Excellent attention to detail.
  • Proven proofreading ability.
  • Ability to work with web-based applications.
  • Familiarity with social media.
  • Experience or familiarity with data management systems.

Artificial Intelligence and Digital Skills

The position also highlights familiarity with conversational AI applications such as:

  • Copilot;
  • Claude;
  • ChatGPT; and
  • Gemini.

Knowledge of collaborative tools such as MURAL, Zoom, Microsoft Teams and Google Forms is also relevant.

Knowledge of design applications such as Canva and Gamma is considered advantageous.

This makes the opportunity particularly interesting for applicants who can combine academic knowledge in disaster-related fields with practical digital and communications skills.

Core Competencies UNDP Is Looking For

Successful candidates should demonstrate several important competencies.

Initiative

Applicants should be capable of working independently, identifying opportunities and taking appropriate action without requiring constant supervision.

Collaboration

The intern should be able to work effectively within a multicultural and multidisciplinary environment, which is essential in an international organisation such as the UNDP.

Communication

Strong written and verbal communication skills are required because the role involves research outputs, presentations, briefs, webinars, knowledge products, and communications materials.

Attention to Detail

The ability to produce accurate, clear, and well-structured work is important, particularly when preparing research, policy, and communications materials.

Organisation

The intern will potentially manage several assignments and priorities, making strong organisational and time-management abilities essential.

Language Requirements

Fluency in written and spoken English is required.

Knowledge of another UN official language is considered an asset.

Applicants who possess additional UN language skills may therefore have an advantage, although English is the stated required language.

What Benefits Does the UNDP Internship Offer?

One of the notable features of this internship is the provision for financial support through a stipend.

Where an intern is not financially supported by a university, government, foundation, scholarship programme or another institution, UNDP will provide a stipend intended to help cover basic daily expenses associated with the internship.

The monthly amount will be determined according to applicable UNDP internship policies and duty-station rates. Where an external funding source provides financial support, UNDP may, subject to applicable rules, pay the difference between that support and the applicable UNDP stipend.

Part-time arrangements are prorated where applicable.

Interns will also accrue combined sick and annual leave at the applicable monthly rate, with part-time arrangements prorated where relevant.

Why This Internship Could Be Valuable for Your Career

The UNDP Early Warning & Preparedness Internship brings together several increasingly important areas of international development.

Exposure to Disaster Risk Reduction

The internship provides practical exposure to disaster risk reduction and preparedness work within a UN organisation.

Experience With Emerging Technologies

The role specifically touches on artificial intelligence, machine learning, predictive analytics, digital twins, remote sensing, geospatial intelligence, risk modelling and data visualisation.

International Development Experience

Working with the Disaster Risk Reduction and Recovery Team provides an opportunity to understand how international development organisations support governments and partners in building resilience.

Research and Analytical Development

Interns can strengthen their ability to research emerging issues, analyse information, identify trends and turn findings into useful knowledge products.

Communications Experience

The position includes preparation of briefs, presentations, talking points, policy materials, social media kits, webinar reports, and other communications products.

Knowledge Management and Learning

The Preparedness Learning Pathway component can provide practical experience in organising resources, developing learning materials, and supporting online learning activities.

Multicultural Collaboration

The role involves collaboration within a multicultural and multidisciplinary environment, helping interns develop experience relevant to future careers in international organisations, development agencies, research institutions, and humanitarian organisations.

What Documents Are Required When Applying?

Applicants are required to submit:

  1. A brief cover letter in English explaining why they want to be considered for the internship.
  2. A current CV in English.

Importantly, the cover letter and CV must be combined into one PDF document, because the application system permits only one document upload.

Documents Successful Candidates May Need to Provide

Candidates who are selected may subsequently be requested to provide electronic copies of supporting documentation, including:

  • Most recent curriculum vitae.
  • A letter from the university confirming current enrolment and graduation date, where applicable.
  • Recent graduation certificate, where applicable.
  • Letter of recommendation from a professor.
  • School transcript.
  • Passport.
  • Medical Certificate of Good Health.
  • Proof of medical insurance coverage.

Applicants should therefore ensure that their academic and identification documents are readily available should they progress through the selection process.

Application Deadline

The deadline for the UNDP Early Warning & Preparedness Internship is:

1 September 2026 at 4:45 PM.

Applicants are encouraged to submit their applications before the final hours to avoid potential technical or submission-related difficulties.

How to Apply for the UNDP Early Warning & Preparedness Internship

Interested and suitably qualified candidates should apply through the official UNDP recruitment portal for Job Identification 35990.

Before submitting an application, candidates should carefully review the eligibility requirements and ensure that their CV and cover letter clearly demonstrate their relevance to the internship.

A strong application should make the connection between the applicant’s:

  • Academic background;
  • Disaster risk reduction or related interests;
  • Research and analytical abilities;
  • Digital and technology skills;
  • Communication capabilities;
  • Knowledge-management experience;
  • Relevant professional, volunteer, or academic projects; and
  • Interest in UNDP’s work on early warning and preparedness.

APPLY HERE

Additional Information About the Selection Process

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from the vacancy announcement. Applications may also be retained for consideration for other similar positions at the same grade level with comparable educational and experience requirements.

Selected candidates will be subject to reference and background checks and will be expected to comply with UNDP standards and principles.

The UNDP also maintains a zero-tolerance policy towards sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, and abuse of authority.

Who Qualifies for This Opportunity?

Eligible category of people: Students, recent graduates, and postgraduate professional trainees whose academic or professional training is relevant to disaster risk reduction, climate change adaptation, disaster management, or humanitarian affairs.

Academic level

The opportunity is open to candidates who are:

  • In the final year of a relevant Bachelor’s degree;
  • Enrolled in a relevant postgraduate programme such as a Master’s degree or higher;
  • Recent graduates with a relevant degree, provided they can begin the internship within one year of graduation; or
  • Participants in a relevant postgraduate professional traineeship programme.

Nationality, race, and geographic eligibility

The supplied opportunity information does not specify a particular race, nationality, country, region, or continent restriction. The vacancy is presented as a home-based, global opportunity, but applicants should confirm any nationality or location conditions directly in the official UNDP recruitment portal before applying. The source itself does not identify an exclusive eligible country or continent.

Tips for Preparing a Strong Application

Applicants can strengthen their applications by tailoring their documents specifically to the responsibilities listed in the vacancy.

1. Tailor Your CV

Instead of submitting a generic CV, highlight experience connected to:

  • Disaster risk reduction;
  • Climate change;
  • Humanitarian affairs;
  • Research and analysis;
  • AI and digital technologies;
  • Data management;
  • Geospatial technologies;
  • Communications;
  • Knowledge management;
  • Social media;
  • Webinar coordination; and
  • Development or humanitarian programming.

2. Connect Your Cover Letter to UNDP’s Priorities

The cover letter should clearly explain why the applicant is interested in early warning, preparedness, risk intelligence, and disaster risk reduction.

Applicants should demonstrate how their academic background, technical skills, and career objectives align with the internship.

3. Demonstrate Digital Competence

Since the position highlights AI, digital applications, data ecosystems, and collaborative technologies, applicants should clearly identify relevant tools and projects they have worked with.

Where applicable, candidates can highlight familiarity with tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, Gemini, MURAL, Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Google Forms, Canva, and Gamma.

4. Show Evidence of Research Ability

Rather than simply stating “excellent research skills,” applicants should demonstrate research experience through academic projects, professional assignments, publications, reports, policy briefs, dissertations, or other relevant work.

5. Highlight Communication Skills

The role involves numerous communications outputs. Candidates should therefore demonstrate their ability to prepare:

  • Reports;
  • Briefing notes;
  • Presentations;
  • Policy briefs;
  • Concept notes;
  • Social media materials;
  • Research summaries; and
  • Other professional communications products.

Visit HERE for more information about the UNDP Early Warning & Preparedness Internship 2026.

Conclusion

The UNDP Early Warning & Preparedness Internship 2026 presents an opportunity for students, recent graduates, and professional trainees to gain practical experience at the intersection of disaster risk reduction, early warning, preparedness, artificial intelligence, digital innovation, research, knowledge management, and international development.

The six-month home-based internship is particularly relevant to candidates pursuing studies or careers in disaster risk reduction, climate change adaptation, disaster management, or humanitarian affairs. At the same time, the position values strong communication, research, analytical, organisational and digital skills.

With responsibilities ranging from analysing AI-powered risk intelligence applications and supporting UNDP’s Preparedness Learning Pathway to preparing communications materials, webinars, presentations, and research products, the internship offers a broad professional learning experience.

Interested candidates should ensure that they meet the educational requirements, prepare a strong CV and cover letter in English, combine both documents into a single PDF, and submit their application through the official recruitment portal before 1 September 2026 at 4:45 PM.

The opportunity may be especially valuable for emerging professionals seeking to build experience in the UN system while contributing to global efforts to strengthen disaster preparedness, resilience, and risk-informed development.
